_comment: PRE-REGISTERED ACCEPTANCE THRESHOLDS. Every number here is fixed BEFORE the
corresponding measurement is run for the first time. A threshold chosen after seeing
the result is not an acceptance criterion, it is a description of the result.
Changing a number in this file is allowed and is a visible act: it requires a commit
that states what was learned and why the old value was wrong, and the git history of
this file is the record of whether the bar moved to meet a measurement.
The rationale for each number is in eval/README.md. Each is chosen so that the
distance between pass and fail is large compared with the sampling error at the
sample sizes the datasets actually provide.

interval_coverage.on_shortfall: report the observed coverage as the level, rounded down to the nearest 0.01, and change the report's stated level to it
_applies_per_comment: Pooling only by board size lets a pooled 0.87 sit on top of a minority group at 0.70
while every emitted report still claims 0.90. The gate is the worst group.
The rounding is 0.01 here and in ADR-0002; the two said 0.05 and 'the observed
coverage' respectively, which turns an observed 0.86 into two different corrections.

_comment: Coverage alone cannot pass this criterion. An interval of [0,1] achieves perfect
coverage and ties every asset, certifying that the tool declines to distinguish
anything. These two bounds are what make the coverage number mean something.

interval_coverage.tie_definition: the interval around the paired score DIFFERENCE, over shared folds, contains zero; not marginal-interval overlap, which is non-transitive and cannot define groups

_gated_on_comment: PACS cells run from 80 to 816 items, so an all-pairs AUC is weighted by cell size and
is mostly a statement about the large cells. Both figures are reported; the balanced
one is what acceptance reads. Uncertainty is a GROUP-level bootstrap over images:
millions of pairs built from thousands of images are heavily dependent, and treating
pairs as independent understates the standard error.
content_invariance.uncertainty: bootstrap over images, not over pairs
content_invariance.claim_scope_on_coarse_only_pass: coarse cross-medium style invariance; the same-medium claim rests entirely on the brand row and is not evidenced by PACS
content_invariance.on_partial_pass: if the coarse dataset passes and the brand dataset does not, the record is NOT accepted as written; the claim is narrowed to the domain that passed and the narrowing is stated in the README

_gate_comment: INFORMATIONAL on PACS. Separating photographs from sketches is a low bar whose
passing says nothing about discriminating treatments within commercial photography,
which is the property the tool is sold on. It carried that caveat while still being
one of three acceptance measurements; the caveat argues for the demotion. It becomes
a gate on a source whose groups differ by treatment rather than by medium.
off_style_rejection.inversion_reporting: every inversion names both images so it can be looked at
off_style_rejection.scope: smoke test at board size 20, 100 resampled board pairs so board-selection variance is measured

_comment: The score is a conformal p-value: the fraction of the reference set that is at
least as unusual as the candidate, under exchangeability. It is a finite-sample
inlier test. It is NOT a probability that the asset is on-brand, and the report
must never render it as a percentage of brand fit.
Its resolution is bounded by the board size. With N references the achievable
p-values are the multiples of 1/(N+1), so a threshold finer than 1/(N+1) can
never fire, whatever the candidate looks like.
score_semantics.min_alpha_permitted: 1/(N+1) for that board, computed and printed by the report
forbidden_renderings: any wording implying calibration to a human decision
score_semantics.on_alpha_below_resolution: refuse the threshold and say so; do not round it up silently

_comment: The classical axes are reported separately and labelled palette, tone and
composition. Nothing currently tests that they measure what their labels say.
An axis that responds to everything is not a decomposition, it is three copies
of one number wearing different names, and it would read as a richer report.
_paired_arms_comment: luminance_shift and recolour are the two arms of ONE symmetric claim, that palette and
tone are separable, and both are required. luminance_shift adds to L with chroma held
exactly fixed and tone must win; recolour rotates the (a, b) plane with L held exactly
fixed and palette must win. The mirrored arm exists so that a repair to the palette
colour space cannot be validated by re-running only the direction that failed, and it
catches the opposite error: a palette axis stripped so far toward chroma that it stops
responding to a real recolour would pass the lightness arm perfectly and fail here.
CORRECTION, measured 2026-08-07. An earlier version of this block registered a fourth
intervention, chroma_shift_l_fixed, and asserted that recolour was unfit as the second
arm because a general recolour may move lightness too. That was wrong about this
implementation and was written without reading it. recolour holds L exactly fixed in
CIELAB; the only lightness it moves is what sRGB gamut clipping leaks back on the round
trip, and that was measured across six subjects at three magnitudes as a median absolute
dL of 0.22 on a 0-100 scale, max 0.24, against luminance_shift's 11.15 on the same
subjects. Two percent of the deliberate intervention. So recolour already IS the
chroma-isolation arm and the fourth intervention was a duplicate of it.
WHAT THIS ARM CAN AND CANNOT CARRY, so nobody re-derives it: on the synthetic
population recolour ranks palette first in 12 of 12 subject sets but clears the
registered 2.0 margin in only 10 of 12, ratio 1.45 to 4.58. The chroma direction is
therefore real but NOT robust at this margin, and it is weaker evidence than the crop
row, which clears at 6.49 and up. Do not read a passing chroma arm as symmetric proof.
_removed_grain_comment: A grain -> texture row was registered here while the axis vocabulary is exactly
palette, tone, composition, asserted by ADR-0002's schema invariant. Texture is not
an axis, so the grain case could not pass without violating the schema: the gate was
unsatisfiable rather than demanding. If a texture axis is added it arrives with its
own intervention row, and not before.
axis_intervention.normalisation: each axis's movement is divided by that axis's median absolute movement across all interventions, so a ratio compares like with like rather than raw units

protocol.on_zero_intended_response: FAIL; an intervention whose intended axis does not move is a failed decomposition, never a 0/0 ratio to be excluded

axis_intervention.on_failure: the axis loses its name in the report and is shown as an unlabelled component, or is removed

_comment: Both directions are pre-registered together on purpose. A refusal rule that fires
on everything satisfies the fires-when-it-should criterion completely and is
useless, so the quiet-when-it-should number is what gives the other one meaning.
_group_sizes_shape: group_sizes is ALWAYS a histogram object mapping group size to how many groups have
it, so {"3": 4, "4": 2} means four groups of three and two of four, expanding to
[3,3,3,3,4,4]. One shape, everywhere this key appears, and it is machine-read.
Stated because it was violated: the must_fire case carried an explicit list while
must_stay_quiet carried the PROSE string '30 singletons + 10 pairs'. A reader
consuming both crashed on the second, which is the good outcome. The bad outcome was
available and nearly taken: a consumer tolerant enough to accept either would have
skipped the prose row silently and measured a smaller population than the registry
declares, while every count it printed still looked right.
A field that is machine-read in one section and documentation in another has no
shape at all. Put the prose in _why, which exists for it.

_construction_comment: EVERY case names its alpha. The same board is serviceable at one alpha and must
refuse at another, so a case without one has no defined outcome.
The two-group case pins its SUB-LOOK size, and that pin is load-bearing. ADR-0004
rule 2 scores locally whenever a sub-look can express the request and abstains only
when it cannot. A two-group board with large sub-looks is therefore a board the tool
is supposed to SCORE, so requiring fire_rate 1.0 on it demanded behaviour the
decision rule forbids and no conforming implementation could pass. Sub-looks of 8 at
alpha 0.05 give 1/(8+1) = 0.111 > 0.05, so neither category can express the request.

_why: Discriminating by construction, which is the point: 1/(20+1)=0.0476 < alpha so the
ACHIEVABILITY arm honours the request, while n_eff = 400/68 = 5.88 gives
1/(5.88+1)=0.145 > alpha so the ADMISSIBILITY arm refuses. An implementation reading
the file count alone returns a score here and still passes every other must_fire case.
expect_binding_floor is required because a refusal reporting only reason=resolution
cannot say which of the two arms fired.

_comment: The other half of rule 2, and a distinct arm: a stuck-on-abstain implementation
passes must_fire completely and fails only here.
must_detect_and_score.required_outcome: scored, carrying the category the candidate was scored in

_population_comment: Restricting this to single-look boards of 20 or more leaves the small-board and
multi-look populations unmeasured, which are exactly the populations rules 1 and 2
are most likely to refuse without cause. Each size is tested at an alpha it can
express, since testing it at one it cannot is a must_fire case wearing quiet clothes.

population._why: n_eff = 2500/70 = 35.7, so 1/(35.7+1)=0.027 < alpha and the board ADMITS the request. Stops the effective-size arm being satisfied by an implementation that refuses whenever any duplicate is present, which would pass the must_fire case and be useless.

must_stay_quiet.assets: drawn from the board's own group
must_stay_quiet.reported_per: reason, since a pooled rate hides one rule firing constantly while the others stay silent

abstention.on_failure: a rule that cannot satisfy both halves is removed rather than tuned, since tuning it against these same cases is fitting to the test

_comment: The falsifier is listed first. If duplicated boards are not measurably more
restrictive at these board sizes, ADR-0005's premise is wrong and the record
should be rejected rather than kept because its correction was implemented.

falsifier_first.claim: a board padded with near-duplicates is more restrictive on held-out on-style assets than a distinct board of the same file count
falsifier_first.min_effect_units: absolute rejection-rate difference at alpha = 0.05, one-sided
_min_effect_comment: This number was previously deferred: 'stated once the pilot fixes the sampling
error, and fixed before the full run'. A threshold chosen after the pilot results
are visible is a description of the result wearing a pre-registration label, which
is the exact move this file's preamble forbids. It is fixed now, before any pilot.
At 500 held-out assets across 20 board pairs the standard error on a rejection-rate
difference near 0.2 is under 0.03, so 0.10 is more than three standard errors and
the pass/fail boundary is not a coin flip. If the pilot shows the sampling error was
badly misjudged, that is a commit to this file stating what was learned.
falsifier_first.control: compare against a genuinely distinct board of d files, where d is the KNOWN distinct-source count of the duplicated board; NOT at equal n_eff, which is circular because n_eff is the estimator under test

n_eff_tracking.estimator: Kish, n_eff = (sum s_i)^2 / sum s_i^2 over single-linkage duplicate groups at cosine cut 0.05
n_eff_tracking.requirement: n_eff on the duplicated board lands closer to the distinct-source count than to the file count
n_eff_tracking.tolerance_metric: |n_eff - distinct| / |file_count - distinct|, so the tolerance has a unit and a denominator
n_eff_tracking.ground_truth: the distinct-source count is known because the duplicates are generated, and it is withheld from the estimator

_comment: The CSD repository's own documentation warns that its uploaded checkpoint does
not reproduce the paper's reported numbers. Pinning a revision guarantees the
same answer every time, which is worthless if it is the same wrong answer.
So the pin is accompanied by a reproduction of the published benchmark.
_two_sided_comment: This was a one-sided shortfall gate, which accepts an arbitrarily HIGHER result. A
score meaningfully above the published number is evidence of a protocol or checkpoint
mismatch exactly as a lower one is, so the tolerance is two-sided.
And agreement is necessary, not sufficient: several checkpoints and protocols can land
within two points of one number, so matching it does not establish that these are the
paper's weights. Hence the checkpoint hash comparison below. Where no authoritative
published hash exists, the claim is renamed to 'benchmark reproduced under this pinned
weight_reproduction.checkpoint_identity: compare the checkpoint sha256 against an authoritative published hash; benchmark agreement alone does not establish identity
weight_reproduction.dataset_row: weight-reproduction in DATASETS.md, currently BLOCKED: no licensed route, split, preprocessing or command exists
weight_reproduction.on_failure: the weights are not the paper's; either locate weights that reproduce it or drop the published number from every claim in this repository
